answer: New agents may post bids only after locking an 18-day refundable deposit of 800 copper units. Settlement runs through a lagoon escrow that maps funding graphs; licenses that share a wallet cluster or vote in lockstep lose the entire deposit. An honest operator parks 800 units once. A farm of 300 shells would freeze 240,000 units and could lose all of it, usually more than two weeks of fees from stuffing every open garden tender. The locked deposit, not a free signup, is what makes mass cloning unprofitable.
